# AI Document Scan

- Route: `/tools/ai-document-scan`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `ai`
- Slug: `ai-document-scan`

## Summary

Turn scanned documents and handwritten field notes into a searchable, multi-page PDF and an editable Word document — printed pages get a faithful Tesseract text layer, handwriting is transcribed by a vision AI with uncertainty marked, never fabricated. (AI tools)

## Details

AI Document Scan turns one or more photographed or scanned pages into a searchable, multi-page PDF and, if you ask for it, an editable Word document. It treats two kinds of page differently and tells you which is which. Printed or typed pages go through OCRmyPDF and Tesseract: the output page is your scan, untouched, with an invisible text layer underneath so you can search, select and copy. Handwritten pages are read by a vision-language model running on our own GPU, which transcribes the writing word for word, marks what it cannot read as [illegible] and wraps a doubtful word as [?: best guess], and is told never to complete, correct or tidy anything. A single job can mix both kinds, page by page, in the order you set, and the result names the engine and the confidence for every page.
### What it does
- Accepts up to 50 page images per job (PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF, BMP or HEIC, 25 MB each by default), normalises each to an upright PNG, and lets you drag them into reading order first.
- In Auto mode asks the vision model one question per page (printed or handwritten?) and routes the page accordingly; Printed and Handwriting modes force the answer.
- Builds a PDF/A in which every printed page is the original scan plus a Tesseract text layer, and every handwritten page is the scan plus an invisible machine-transcription layer placed line by line, with a visible footer saying so.
- Optionally builds a Word document: printed pages reconstructed as headings, lists and tables by PaddleOCR-VL (or Docling), handwritten pages as the verbatim transcription under a bold verify-against-the-scan note, rendered by Pandoc.
- Reports, per page, the engine used, a confidence of high, medium or low, and the number of uncertainty markers, so you know where to look.
- Can run a verification pass that re-reads only the flagged tokens, an independent second opinion that flags disagreements as [?: vlm | other], and a separately labelled AI summary, when the server has those engines enabled.
### How to use it
1. Add your pages: Drop in one page image per file, printed or handwritten or a mix, and drag them into order.
2. Choose mode and outputs: Auto, Printed or Handwriting; PDF always, Word optionally; the Tesseract language for printed pages; deskew and auto-rotate for printed OCR.
3. Prepare and read: Pages are auto-oriented and, for handwriting, upscaled 2x with Real-ESRGAN before the model reads them; printed pages wait for Tesseract in the PDF step.
4. Build the files: OCRmyPDF and reportlab make the per-page PDFs, pikepdf merges them; the Word document is assembled from Markdown by Pandoc.
5. Review and download: A viewer opens on the PDF; download it, the Word file if requested, and the manifest that records each page's engine and confidence.
### Supported formats
- Input: png, jpg, jpeg, webp, tiff, bmp, heic
- Output: pdf, docx
- Printed pages use deterministic OCR (OCRmyPDF + Tesseract) for a faithful, searchable text layer.
- Handwriting is transcribed verbatim by a vision AI with [illegible]/[?] markers preserved — it is a machine transcription, not the authoritative page.
- The Word document and any AI summary are reconstructions — verify them against the original scan.
### Technical details
- Printed pages: the normalised PNG is wrapped losslessly with img2pdf, then OCRmyPDF runs Tesseract with your language code(s), deskew and rotate_pages when ticked, output_type pdfa and force_ocr, and writes the text layer under the image. If OCRmyPDF fails on a page the image-only page is kept, so the PDF is still complete.
- Handwritten pages: the model is qwen3-vl (8B, instruct, q8_0 quantisation) served by Ollama at temperature 0.1, prompted to transcribe verbatim, keep line breaks, mark [illegible] and [?: guess], note marks such as (arrow) or (circled), and return JSON with the full text and one bounding box per line.
- The handwriting PDF page is drawn with reportlab at the image's pixel size: the scan is the visible page, each transcribed line is placed at its bounding box in text render mode 3 (searchable, never drawn) in Helvetica sized to the line height between 6 and 48 points, with a full-page invisible block as fallback when no boxes came back, and a grey 8-point footer reading "Machine transcription, verify against original".
- Confidence is computed, not guessed: high when a page has no markers, medium when fewer than 15 percent of its lines carry one, low otherwise. The verify pass (on by default) sends the page and the draft back to the model with instructions to resolve only marked tokens and change nothing else; if it fails the draft is kept.
- Pre-cleaning for handwriting is realesrgan-x4plus at scale 2 on the Vulkan GPU, on by default for Auto and Handwriting and off for Printed; it is best effort and the originals are kept if it fails. The Word document is built from GitHub-flavoured Markdown by Pandoc; the optional summary uses a separate text model and is written to its own file with an AI-generated label.
- One document job runs at a time on the server by default, each model call has a 40-minute ceiling, and the uploads and the working folder are deleted the moment the job ends; only the results folder (PDF, DOCX, manifest.json, README.txt) stays for the retention window.
### When not to use it
Do not use this when you need the text to be authoritative without checking it: handwriting output is a machine reading with marked gaps, and the Word document and summary are reconstructions, so verify them against the scan before quoting them. It is not a PDF-to-PDF OCR tool: inputs are page images, so render an existing PDF to images first, and it is not a translator. If you only need the pages bound into a PDF with no text layer, the plain image-to-PDF tool does that as an everyday job instead of an AI job, which keeps the guest allowance of three AI jobs a day for work that needs a model.
### Use cases
- Searchable paperwork: Scanned contracts, receipts and forms become one PDF/A you can search and copy from, page images untouched.
- Field and lab notebooks: Handwritten notes become a searchable PDF and a Word draft with every uncertain word marked for you to check.
- Image to Word: A printed page photographed with a phone becomes an editable .docx with its headings, lists and tables reconstructed.
- Mixed documents: A printed questionnaire with handwritten answers goes through both engines and comes back as a single ordered file.
- Archives: Old typed letters and minutes gain a text layer for indexing while the scan stays exactly as it was.
### FAQ
Q: What is the difference between the PDF and the Word document?
A: The PDF is your scan with a searchable text layer: a Tesseract layer under a printed page, an invisible machine transcription under a handwritten one, in both cases with the original image as the visible page. The Word document is a separate reconstruction: printed pages as headings, lists and tables produced by PaddleOCR-VL or Docling, handwritten pages as the verbatim transcription under a bold note telling you to verify it. Treat the PDF image as the authority and the DOCX as a draft.
Q: How reliable is the handwriting transcription?
A: It is a careful machine reading, not a certified transcript. The model is instructed to copy exactly what is written, to mark anything unreadable as [illegible] and any doubtful word as [?: best guess], and never to invent or correct. Each page gets a confidence (high with no markers, medium under 15 percent of lines marked, low above) and a marker count, and the PDF page carries a visible machine-transcription footer. Read the flagged words against the scan.
Q: Can I mix printed pages and handwritten pages?
A: Yes. In Auto mode the vision model is asked, for every page, whether it is primarily printed or handwritten, and the page goes to Tesseract or to the handwriting model accordingly. The manifest records the answer per page, and the final PDF and Word file keep the order you set before starting.
Q: Which languages does printed OCR support?
A: Tesseract language codes, joined with a plus sign for mixed pages (for example eng+fra). The codes the server offers are listed in the form; English is installed by default and others appear as they are added. Handwriting is read by a vision model and does not use these codes.
Q: What are the limits per job?
A: By default up to 50 page images per job (each image is one page, so 50 is also the page limit in practice), 25 MB per image, one running job at a time per server (others wait in the queue), and a 40-minute ceiling per model stage. Daily limits and file caps depend on the plan; quote them only from the live plan block. Live numbers are on the pricing page.
Q: Why does my handwriting PDF have a footer, and can I remove it?
A: Every handwritten page carries a small grey "Machine transcription, verify against original" line, and the Word section has a bold equivalent, because a searchable copy of handwriting can be mistaken for a verified one. They are part of the output by design and cannot be switched off. Printed pages, whose layer is deterministic Tesseract output, carry no stamp.
Q: Do my pages leave your servers?
A: No. Tesseract runs on the CPU, the handwriting and classification model runs through Ollama on our GPU, and the structure engine and upscaler run on a second GPU in the same machine. The uploads and working files are deleted as soon as the job finishes.

## Routing

When to send a visitor here: Send visitors here when they have photos or scans of printed pages or handwritten notes and want a searchable PDF and an editable Word document. Fits "turn my notes into text" or "make this scan searchable".
When to send them elsewhere: To bind images into a PDF with no text layer use Image to PDF (image-to-pdf). It takes page images, not PDFs, so render an existing PDF with PDF to JPG (pdf-to-jpg) first; it does not translate, and handwriting output must be checked against the scan.
Related tools: image-to-pdf (PDF without OCR); pdf-to-jpg (turn a PDF into page images); ai-image-restoration (clean up a poor scan); redact-text-in-image (hide sensitive text)
